ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Yul Brynner

code.originalText: Biomarker results and start of first-line pembrolizumab

text.paragraph: Tissue sequencing result and start of first-line pembrolizumab. [S]

Mr. Brynner returns one week later. The tissue sequencing report arrived yesterday: KRAS G12V and TP53 mutations, with no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK, HER2, or NRG1 alteration, in agreement with the plasma result. With the thoracic oncologist he chose pembrolizumab alone, given every 3 weeks, rather than with chemotherapy, because it is a preferred first-line option at his PD-L1 level and spares him the fatigue and nausea of chemotherapy while he works toward the stage. His first infusion is this afternoon. The dental examination four days ago found no problems. He is unchanged: weak voice, a little morning cough, no pain, and steady weight. The visit ran long with treatment teaching, and the symptom questionnaire was not completed. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-22; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Slightly reduced breath sounds at the left apex

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, stage IVB (cT4 N2 M1c, AJCC 8th edition), unresectable: the primary invades the mediastinum at the aortopulmonary window; bone metastases; PD-L1 tumor proportion score 70 percent (22C3); ECOG performance status 1; comprehensive genomic profiling results in the notes
S — Synthetic modern histology, stage, and biomarkers linked to his documented inoperable lung cancer of September 1983.
Bone metastases at T10, the right ilium, and the left sixth rib on PET-CT, without pain, fracture, or cord compression
S — Synthetic metastatic sites chosen so that first-line systemic therapy is the standard of care; no source describes the spread of his cancer.
Left vocal fold paralysis with a breathy, weak voice, most likely from left recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement by disease in the aortopulmonary window
S — Synthetic laryngoscopy finding anchored to the published account that a vocal-cord problem led to his diagnosis; the lay 'lump on his vocal cords' is not modeled as a laryngeal tumor.
Left upper lobe mass invading the mediastinum, with enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes, on CT at presentation; suspicious for lung cancer pending tissue diagnosis
S — Synthetic presenting imaging finding, recorded before the tissue diagnosis.
Former smoker: about 3 packs a day from age 12 until he quit 12 years ago, roughly 115 pack-years; no tobacco since
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to the documented heavy smoking and quitting; the pack-year figure is a synthetic midpoint of conflicting published amounts.

Adenocarcinoma of the lung, stage IVB, PD-L1 70 percent, no actionable alteration (C34.12). Biomarker testing complete. With PD-L1 of 50 percent or more and no actionable alteration, pembrolizumab monotherapy is a preferred first-line regimen. Baseline TSH 2.1, free T4 1.2, morning cortisol 14.2, liver tests, glucose, creatinine, calcium, and blood count normal. [S]
Pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously today, then every 3 weeks.
Written list of immune-related warning symptoms and the 24-hour oncology telephone line given.
Laboratory panel before each infusion; response CT about nine weeks after starting.
Zoledronic acid with the second cycle, so that a first-dose reaction is not confused with an early immune-related event.

Bone metastases (C79.51). No pain; dental examination done. [S]
First zoledronic acid dose with cycle 2.

Left vocal fold paralysis (J38.01). Unchanged. [S]

tr.td: At diagnosis of advanced nonsquamous NSCLC: EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS (including G12C), MET exon 14, RET, NTRK, HER2, NRG1, and PD-L1; repeat at progression
Tissue sequencing: KRAS G12V and TP53; no actionable alteration; concordant with plasma
Before each immunotherapy infusion: TSH, liver tests, glucose; cortisol at baseline and as indicated
Baseline: TSH 2.1, free T4 1.2, morning cortisol 14.2, ALT 26, AST 23, alkaline phosphatase 101, bilirubin 0.6, glucose 94, all normal
Blood count, kidney function, and calcium before systemic therapy
Hemoglobin 13.6, white cells 7.6, platelets 284, creatinine 0.9 (eGFR 92), calcium 9.5
Every 6 to 12 weeks on active systemic therapy
First response CT about nine weeks after starting
Distress and symptom screening (NCCN Distress Thermometer, ESAS)
Every visit; at minimum at key transitions

Not done today, at the start of treatment, a key transition: the visit ran long with treatment teaching. Deviation from the every-visit and key-transition screen. No harm resulted: the palliative care team assessed his symptoms and distress in full a week later, and the next scores were lower. Corrective action: the ESAS and distress thermometer are now completed on a tablet at check-in, before the clinician sees him
Tired by evening, unchanged; no daytime naps
Dental evaluation before a bone-modifying agent
Baseline, then periodically on zoledronic acid or denosumab
Examination four days ago: no active disease, no extractions needed
Within eight weeks of diagnosis of advanced cancer
Injection medialization in two weeks; voice therapy started
Every visit during and after platinum or taxane
Pembrolizumab alone; no platinum or taxane

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, lung cancer monograph (2026); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (2026); Management of Immune-Related Adverse Events in Patients Treated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: ASCO Guideline Update (2021); Integration of Palliative Care Into Standard Oncology Care: American Society of Clinical Oncology Clinical Practice Guideline Update (2017); NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Distress Management (2026)

Follow-up: First pembrolizumab infusion this afternoon. Palliative care next week. Voice injection in two weeks. Cycle 2 in three weeks with the laboratory panel and the first zoledronic acid dose. Call the oncology line for any warning symptom. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-13: cycle 2 review: immune-related adverse event monitoring, symptoms, and return to work. [S]
